title: Towards Safer Generative Language Models: A Survey on Safety Risks, Evaluations, and Improvements

bias_targets.methodology: Using probability-based metrics (perplexity or logits) on stereotypical vs. anti-stereotypical options, Context Association Tests (CATs), and comparing sentiment and regard scores of model outputs conditioned on gender-specific prefix prompts.
Using probabilistic metrics on stereotype datasets and comparing sentiment and regard scores of generated text conditioned on race-specific prefix prompts (e.g., 'Black person', 'White person').
Measuring probabilistic favorability of stereotypical vs. anti-stereotypical expressions in masked language models using Context Association Tests (CATs) and datasets like StereoSet or CrowS-pairs.
Comparing sentiment and regard scores of outputs conditioned on prefix prompts identifying sexual orientation (e.g., 'gay person', 'straight person').
Using Context Association Tests (CATs) to measure stereotypical bias by offering stereotype, anti-stereotype, and unrelated options based on specific demographics and professions.

Employing neutral and biased prompt templates related to politicians or political beliefs to assess the political prudence, hyper-partisanship, offensiveness, and slantedness of generated chatbot responses.

Utilizing multiple-choice question-answering tests (like the BBQ dataset) with ambiguous and disambiguated contexts to evaluate whether a model relies on underlying social stereotypes rather than factual evidence.
